# Noise robustness of the extraction (generated by `python -m app.eval.noise_robustness`; do not edit by hand)

Gold: `.runtime/bench/coding/latent.json`, the facts the `coding` branch's generator sampled before rendering each CV (seed 42); this tool never changes them. Noisy inputs: `.runtime/bench/coding_noise/<kind>_<level>/cvs/` (text) and `…/pdf/` (the same text as a PDF). Seed 42 per (kind, level, CV). `original` = the generator's 200 CVs as rendered (its 7 noisy CVs included) and must match `docs/EXTRACTION_RESULTS.md`; the noise rows use the 193 clean CVs (`accents`: the clean Vietnamese ones). `ocr` here is simulated character confusion; the real PaddleOCR run is `docs/OCR_RESULTS.md`.

**Quick run:** a seeded random sample of 60 of the 200 CVs (seed 42), and the ranking table for `original` and `char 0.05` only. A full run omits `--sample`.

## 3. Ranking on the PDF-read CVs: coding benchmark, 6 JDs, mean nDCG@10

All 200 CVs in the pool; the noise applies as in the tables above and leaves the other CVs unchanged. Systems without LLM judgement; JD requirements from `.runtime/eval/requirements/coding/`. PDFs: `…/<kind>_<level>/pdf_pool/`.

| noise | level | B0 BM25 | Δ vs original | B3 8-axis ⊕ CE [hybrid] | Δ vs original |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| original | 0 | **0.540** | +0.000 | **0.788** | +0.000 |
| char | 0.05 | **0.400** | -0.140 | **0.612** | -0.176 |

## Reading the tables

- *years MAE* is over the CVs where a date range was still found, so it can fall as noise rises (only the easy CVs remain); read it with *years found* and *years within 1 y (of all CVs)*.
- *flagged for review* is the X10 quality gate: the share of CVs sent to HR or the investigator (N12) instead of being scored silently.
- A PII leak counts a name or gender value from the original CV that is still in the text the pipeline indexes after redaction.
- A PDF wraps long lines, so `layout` noise (lost line breaks) comes back with breaks at wrap points, as a real exported CV would.
